note: How the scenario moves a rating. Read by src/lib/score.js. Every rule here fires on data the tool already holds: the fetched weapon stats, the game own tags, or fields curated in items.json. Nothing here is a hand written per item list. A rule states a delta in points, where roughly 14 points is one tier, or scales one from a number the game publishes. Every rule must carry a `say`, because a score that cannot explain itself is a score nobody should trust. And every rule must fire on something that actually varies with the scenario, which is the test the armour rules failed.
whyThereAreNoArmourRules: There were five, added in 1.10.0 and removed in 1.13.0, and they were the wrong altitude. Measured on the Automaton front, 48 of 51 primaries shared one of two identical armour readings and 42 of them lost a tier for it. A rule that fires the same way on 94% of a population is not telling you anything about any of them. The deeper error: a community tier already prices in what an item is for. Voters know an assault rifle does not open a Hulk, so the Liberator's B on bots is a B given that it is a chaff gun, and penalising it again charges twice for one fact. The test to apply to any replacement is whether the thing it fires on actually varies with the scenario. Armour reach per item does not; it is constant, and only the front and difficulty move it, which moves every primary together. That makes it a loadout property. src/lib/squad.js already had this right, asking whether anyone in the squad carries AP 4 or better rather than judging each weapon alone, and that is the shape armour scoring should come back in.
sourceOfHazardWording: The hazard mechanics quoted in these sentences come from the helldivers-2/json community dataset, MIT licensed. They are the game's own descriptions, not our guesses.

rules.name: Cold lets heat weapons fire longer
rules.say: Icy temperatures delay heat buildup, so this fires longer before it vents. The game publishes the figure per weapon and this one is above average.

rules.name: Heat makes heat weapons overheat sooner
rules.say: High temperatures speed up heat buildup, so this overheats sooner than it does anywhere else.

rules.name: Cold slows fast firing weapons
rules.say: Cold reduces rate of fire, and a weapon that leans on a high rate of fire feels that more than a slow one does.

rules.name: Ion storms can stop a call-in arriving
rules.say: Ion storms intermittently disable Stratagems. Anything you have to call in can simply not arrive.

rules.name: Ion storms favour what you carry
rules.say: Ion storms cannot switch off what is already in your hands, which is worth more here than it usually is.

rules.name: Sandstorms blind marksman rifles
rules.say: Sandstorms greatly reduce visibility while they last, and range stops being an advantage. They are weather rather than climate though: roughly three minutes at a time, so this is a risk you carry rather than a state you are in.

rules.name: Sandstorms blind long range support weapons
rules.say: Sandstorms greatly reduce visibility while they last, and range stops being an advantage. They are weather rather than climate though: roughly three minutes at a time, so this is a risk you carry rather than a state you are in.
rules.judgement: Our call, not a sourced field. It rides on the long-range tag on the items now rather than being listed again in every rule that wants it, and vocabulary.json records the reasoning. Nothing published separates a long range support weapon from a close one: projectile velocity does not, since laser weapons read 1300 and assault rifles read 820.

rules.name: Sandstorms favour close range
rules.say: Sandstorms greatly reduce visibility, which drags every fight to the range this already wants.

rules.name: Blizzards blind marksman rifles
rules.say: Blizzards moderately reduce visibility while they blow, which costs a long range weapon most of what it is for. They pass, so this is a risk you carry rather than a state you are in.

rules.name: Blizzards blind long range support weapons
rules.say: Blizzards moderately reduce visibility while they blow, which costs a long range weapon most of what it is for. They pass, so this is a risk you carry rather than a state you are in.
rules.judgement: Our call, not a sourced field. It rides on the long-range tag on the items now rather than being listed again in every rule that wants it, and vocabulary.json records the reasoning. Nothing published separates a long range support weapon from a close one: projectile velocity does not, since laser weapons read 1300 and assault rifles read 820.

rules.name: Blizzards favour close range
rules.say: Blizzards moderately reduce visibility, so engagements start closer than you would choose.

rules.name: Fog dims marksman rifles
rules.say: Thick fog lightly reduces visibility. Less punishing than a storm, but a marksman weapon still loses some of its reach.

rules.name: Fog dims long range support weapons
rules.say: Thick fog lightly reduces visibility. Less punishing than a storm, but a marksman weapon still loses some of its reach.
rules.judgement: Our call, not a sourced field. It rides on the long-range tag on the items now rather than being listed again in every rule that wants it, and vocabulary.json records the reasoning. Nothing published separates a long range support weapon from a close one: projectile velocity does not, since laser weapons read 1300 and assault rifles read 820.

rules.name: Tremors punish a standing reload
rules.say: Tremors stun players and enemies alike, and this cannot be reloaded on the move. Being stunned mid reload is how a fight gets away from you.

rules.name: Tremors punish emplacements
rules.say: Tremors stun anything standing on the ground, including you while you are setting this up.

rules.name: Fire tornadoes and fire kits
rules.say: The planet is already on fire. Adding to it makes telling your fire from the planet's harder, and fire resist armor is doing double duty.

rules.name: Acid storms weaken armour passives
rules.say: Acid storms temporarily reduce armor effectiveness for everyone, so a passive that leans on staying alive through damage is worth a little less.

rules.name: Terminids reward durable damage
rules.say: Terminids are mostly large fleshy parts, and durable damage is what hurts those. This one keeps most of its damage against them where a chaff gun loses it.

rules.name: Terminids punish light damage
rules.say: Almost all of this weapon's damage is standard rather than durable, which a Charger's backside and a Spewer's sack largely ignore.

rules.name: Terminids punish slow handling
rules.say: Poor ergonomics means the barrel lags behind the camera, and Hunters do not wait for you to catch up.

rules.name: The Illuminate reward sustained fire
rules.say: The Crusher regenerates while taking heavy damage and has to be worn down without a pause. A deep magazine is how you get one.

rules.name: The Illuminate punish one shot weapons
rules.say: Reloading between shots gives a Crusher the pause it needs to regenerate. Burst damage is worth less on this front than it looks.

rules.name: Demolition missions reward demolition 40
rules.say: Demolition 40 closes a hole or a fabricator from outside, without spending a call-in. On this mission that is the whole job.

rules.name: Demolition missions reward hole closers
rules.say: Closes objectives from your carried kit rather than by burning a stratagem, which is what this mission asks for over and over.

rules.name: Carrying punishes two handed support weapons
rules.say: Carrying the objective means this is on your back, not in your hands, for most of the walk.

rules.name: Escorts reward smoke
rules.say: Smoke breaks the line of sight along the route the civilians have to walk, which is the whole problem this mission sets.

rules.name: Holding ground rewards emplacements
rules.say: One arena and no ground to give up. Anything you can plant and leave finally gets to sit still long enough to pay for itself.

rules.name: Holding ground rewards the Cremator
rules.say: You are not going anywhere and they keep coming. Five hundred rounds of fire fed from your back, poured across the one approach they have to use, is what a held position is for.
rules.judgement: Ours, the curator's call of 4 October 2026: the Cremator shines in Eradicate and defence missions, huddled on a position against large groups. Deliberately not a front rule: the vote already prices how well fire does against bugs and bots, and a second bump for the same fact would count it twice. Named by id because no published field separates a backpack fed stream from a flamethrower that reloads.

rules.name: High value targets reward anti-tank
rules.say: A set number of named heavies and nothing else counts, so opening heavy armor is the entire loadout question.

rules.name: Blitz rewards fast demolition
rules.say: Twelve minutes and a map full of structures. Closing one from outside, without lining up a throw, is what the clock rewards.

rules.name: Carrying rewards a one handed sidearm
rules.say: You will have an objective in one hand for most of this mission. A one handed weapon lets you shoot while carrying it; everything else means putting it down first. It does not make a bad sidearm good, it makes a good one indispensable.

rules.name: Carrying rewards a one handed SMG
rules.say: You will have an objective in one hand for most of this mission. A one handed weapon lets you shoot while carrying it; everything else means putting it down first. It does not make a bad sidearm good, it makes a good one indispensable.

rules.name: Alone or in pairs on a hard bot drop, quiet wins
rules.say: One or two of you, at a level where every fight you start is one you have to finish alone. A suppressed weapon is audible at 13 metres rather than 100, so a sentry on a perimeter dies without waking the base behind it.
rules.source: The five suppressed weapons. Sourced rather than judged: the wiki carries Suppressed as a trait in each weapon's infobox and its Stealth page gives the audible range as 13 metres. A tag rather than a fetched field because the fetch reads only reload times from weapon infoboxes so far
rules.judgement: Ours, retuned on 4 October 2026 at the curator's word: a four stack that has reached Super Helldive knows what it is doing, and loud is how most of them play it. So this fires only for one or two of you, from solo on Suicide Mission or two of you on Impossible, and grows to about a tier alone on Super Helldive. It used to fire for every squad, reach a tier at peril 22, where four of you at difficulty 10 sat, and mark silenced weapons down below zero. Both are gone.

rules.name: Alone or in pairs on a very hard bot drop, noise costs
rules.say: With one or two of you this deep, every shot from this brings the patrol and there is nobody holding the line while you deal with it. Still a good gun. The noise is a cost here, not a verdict.
rules.judgement: Ours, cut to a nudge on 4 October 2026: the curator's Autocannon and Leveller clear Super Helldive in a four stack, and this was marking them down there. It now fires only for one or two of you, from solo on Impossible or two of you on Helldive, and never reaches half a tier. It matches nearly half of everything you can hold, so it has to argue quietly.

rules.name: Storms favour stealth for one or two of you on bots
rules.say: A storm cuts their sight as much as yours, and with this few of you this deep you are not trying to win the firefight. Reduced visibility plus a weapon nobody hears is the difference between crossing an outpost and being chased out of one.
rules.judgement: Ours. Stacks with the plain quiet rule, so a storm is worth a little extra on top. Same window as that rule since 4 October 2026.

rules.name: Alone or in pairs on a hard bug or squid drop, quiet helps
rules.say: Stealth works here too: bugs and squids hear and see you the way bots do, and a breach or a Watcher's call you never trigger is a fight you never have. It matters less than on bots, where one flare brings a dropship.
rules.source: helldivers.wiki.gg, Stealth: every faction detects by sound and then sight. Terminids open a breach and the Illuminate need a Watcher to call for help, each with a long cue that can be interrupted
rules.judgement: Ours. About six tenths of the bot rule, because stealth is most viable against the Automatons. Added 4 October 2026.

rules.name: Alone or in pairs on a hard bot drop, stealth armour pays
rules.say: One or two of you this deep, and the patrol that never sees you is the one you never fight. Less noise, a shorter detection range, or both, is a margin of error you will use.
rules.source: The passive's own effect: Reduced Signature cuts movement noise by half and detection range by 40%, Scout the range alone, Feet First the noise alone
rules.judgement: Ours, the curator's window from 4 October 2026: solo from Suicide Mission, two of you from Impossible, growing to nearly a tier alone on Super Helldive. Three or four of you get nothing, because a full squad at any level can hold the fight it starts. All three passives get the same points, and the vote already orders them.

rules.name: Alone or in pairs on a hard bug or squid drop, stealth armour helps
rules.say: Bugs and squids find you by sound and sight too, so not being found still saves you the breach or the Watcher's call. Worth less than against bots, worth something.
rules.source: helldivers.wiki.gg, Stealth
rules.judgement: Ours. Six tenths of the bot rule, the ratio the quiet weapon rules keep.

rules.name: Stealth armour is wasted on an easy drop
rules.say: At this level being heard costs you nothing, so a passive spent on not being heard is a passive not spent on staying alive or carrying more.
rules.judgement: Ours. Only below zero peril, four of you through Challenging or alone on Easy, and never more than half a tier: four of you on Trivial lose about that. The curator: on a low difficulty it can come down.

rules.name: Commando missions refuse reinforcement boosters
rules.say: A Commando mission will not let you bring this. The game refuses reinforcement boosters on them, so the slot is spent on nothing.
rules.source: helldivers.wiki.gg, Commando Missions, read 1 October 2026

rules.name: Commando missions punish call-ins that earn their keep by repeating
rules.say: This earns its rating by coming back every minute or two. On a Commando mission every call-in waits for the Super Destroyer, which is overhead for one minute when you land and once more per Helldiver, so it comes twice at most.
rules.source: helldivers.wiki.gg, Commando Missions, read 1 October 2026

rules.name: Commando missions forgive a long cooldown
rules.say: Every call-in here waits for the same two windows, so a long cooldown costs nothing. What is left is how hard this hits when it lands.
rules.source: helldivers.wiki.gg, Commando Missions, read 1 October 2026

rules.name: Commando missions punish throwaway launchers
rules.say: A throwaway launcher is worth its rating because two more fall every minute. Here they fall only while the Super Destroyer is overhead, twice in the whole mission.
rules.source: helldivers.wiki.gg, Commando Missions, read 1 October 2026

rules.name: Commando missions reward heat weapons, which need no ammo
rules.say: Resupply is a call-in, and here call-ins come twice. This runs on heat rather than magazines: keep it from overheating and it never runs dry, long after everybody else's ammo is gone.
rules.source: helldivers.wiki.gg, Commando Missions, read 1 October 2026
rules.judgement: That ammo runs short follows from resupply being a stratagem. That a weapon needing none is worth a full tier, and almost a given to bring, is the curator's call, 1 October 2026: the Quasar is S+ on these missions, not S.

rules.name: Commando missions reward arc weapons, which need no ammo
rules.say: Resupply is a call-in, and here call-ins come twice. An arc weapon has no ammunition at all, so it keeps working long after everybody else's has run out.
rules.source: helldivers.wiki.gg, Commando Missions, read 1 October 2026
rules.judgement: That ammo runs short follows from resupply being a stratagem. That a weapon needing none is worth a full tier, and almost a given to bring, is the curator's call, 1 October 2026: the Quasar is S+ on these missions, not S.

rules.name: Commando missions reward bringing your own supplies
rules.say: Resupply is a call-in, and here call-ins come twice. Supplies you brought with you are the resupply you will not otherwise get.
rules.source: helldivers.wiki.gg, Commando Missions, read 1 October 2026
rules.judgement: Named by hand: nothing published marks an item as carrying supplies for the squad.

rules.name: Commando missions reward suppressed weapons
rules.say: Every time a bot calls for help the threat level climbs, and the whole map gets worse. A weapon they cannot hear keeps it down.
rules.source: helldivers.wiki.gg, Commando Missions, read 1 October 2026

rules.name: Commando missions reward stealth armour
rules.say: Every time a bot calls for help the threat level climbs, and the whole map gets worse. Not being seen is the best answer to that this mission has.
rules.source: helldivers.wiki.gg, Commando Missions, read 1 October 2026

rules.name: A silenced weapon without stealth armour is half a commitment
rules.say: Nobody hears the shot, and every patrol still sees you coming. Silence pays when you are not spotted first, so without armour that keeps you unseen this is the slower gun for most of its upside.
rules.judgement: Ours, the curator's call of 4 October 2026: go full or go not at all. Only where stealth is worth playing, solo from Suicide Mission or two of you from Impossible. Fires only inside a build.

rules.name: Stealth armour with a silenced weapon is the whole commitment
rules.say: Unseen and unheard. The armour keeps patrols from finding you, and the weapon removes the ones you choose without waking the rest.
rules.judgement: Ours, the other half of the same call, in the same window. Fires only inside a build.

rules.name: True Grit on a support weapon with a long reload
rules.say: This takes three and a half seconds or more to reload, and True Grit takes 30% off it every time. The longer the reload, the more of every fight that is.
rules.source: Reload times from each weapon's own wiki infobox, fetched by npm run wiki. True Grit: +30% support weapon reload speed
rules.judgement: Ours. A magazine over 120 is left out, the Stalwart, Machine Gun and Flamethrower among them: they reload so rarely that a faster reload barely shows. Heat weapons are left out too: the Laser Cannon swaps a heat sink it rarely needs. Fires only inside a build.

rules.name: True Grit on a reload that roots you
rules.say: You cannot move while this reloads, which is the price of how hard it hits. Every second True Grit takes off is a second you are not standing still in the open.
rules.source: Stationary Reload from the weapon's wiki infobox or the game's own tag, whichever says so
rules.judgement: Ours. Stacks with the long reload rule, because a long reload you cannot walk out of is worse than either alone. Fires only inside a build.

rules.name: True Grit on a weapon that reloads after every shot
rules.say: One round in the magazine means a reload after every shot, so 30% off the reload is close to 30% more shots in a fight.
rules.source: Magazine size and reload time from the wiki
rules.judgement: Ours. This is what puts the Railgun and the Speargun on the list: their reloads are short, and they do one after every shot. Fires only inside a build.

rules.name: True Grit on a big belt with a long reload
rules.say: This reloads rarely, but when it does it takes three and a half seconds or more, usually at the worst moment. True Grit takes 30% off that one long reload.
rules.source: Reload times and magazine sizes from each weapon's wiki infobox. True Grit: +30% support weapon reload speed
rules.judgement: Ours, and the curator's correction of 9 October 2026: a big belt reloads rarely, which is why this is a third of the long reload rule, not nothing. Stacks with the stationary rule, which is what puts the Machine Gun above the Stalwart. Fires only inside a build.

rules.name: True Grit with a support weapon worth reloading faster
rules.say: Your support weapon reloads long, often or rooted to the spot, and this passive takes 30% off every one of those. This is what True Grit is for.
rules.judgement: Ours. Fires only inside a build.

rules.name: True Grit with nothing that reloads
rules.say: No support weapon here has a reload for True Grit to shorten: an Arc Thrower or a Quasar never reloads, an expendable is thrown away, and no support weapon is no support weapon. You keep the handling and lose the half that makes it S+.
rules.judgement: Ours. Fires only inside a build.

rules.name: A pistol beside Gunslinger
rules.say: Gunslinger reloads this 40% faster, draws it half again as quick and takes most of its recoil away. A pistol you fight with becomes a pistol you can lean on.
rules.judgement: Ours. The Pistol category only: the Ultimatum, the Grenade Pistol and the Stim Pistol are tools you fire once, not sidearms you fight with. Fires only inside a build.

rules.name: Gunslinger with a pistol worth fighting with
rules.say: You brought a real pistol, and every part of this passive is about it: the reload, the draw and the recoil.
rules.judgement: Ours. Fires only inside a build.

rules.name: Gunslinger with no pistol to sling
rules.say: Every part of Gunslinger is about your sidearm, and this build's sidearm is not a pistol you fight with. A one shot launcher, a stim pistol or a blade gets almost nothing from it.
rules.judgement: Ours. Fires only inside a build.

rules.name: A melee weapon beside armour that hits harder
rules.say: Your armour adds to every swing of this. If you are going to fight up close, this is how.
rules.judgement: Ours. Scales with the armour's melee bonus: Peak Physique and Rock Solid add 40%, Reinforced Epaulettes 20%. Fires only inside a build.

rules.name: Melee armour with a melee weapon to use it on
rules.say: You brought something to swing, and this passive is for exactly that.
rules.judgement: Ours. Scales with the bonus. No penalty without a melee weapon: everyone can melee, and Peak Physique's ergonomics are worth something to any gun. Fires only inside a build.

rules.name: Armour that resists the fire you brought
rules.say: You are bringing fire, and fire spreads to your own feet. This armour takes most of the sting out of standing in your own flames.
rules.source: The passive's own effect, read as a number. Inflammable resists 75%, Kinetic Displacement Mitigation and Acclimated 50%, Desert Stormer 40%
rules.judgement: Ours, the curator's pairing from 4 October 2026. Scales with how much it resists, so a single element passive beats one covering everything at a lower figure. Fires only inside a build.

rules.name: Fire gear is safer with armour that resists it
rules.say: Burning ground and a flame that licks back are this weapon's worst habit, and your armour shrugs most of that off.
rules.judgement: Ours, and deliberately small: the armour does not make the weapon better, it makes its worst habit cheaper. Scales with the armour's figure. Fires only inside a build.

rules.name: Armour that resists the arc you brought
rules.say: You are bringing arc, and arc jumps to whoever is nearest, a Tesla Tower above all. This armour takes most of that off you.
rules.source: The passive's own effect, read as a number. Electrical Conduit resists 95%, Adreno-Defibrillator and Acclimated 50%, Desert Stormer 40%
rules.judgement: Ours, the curator's pairing from 4 October 2026. Scales with how much it resists, so a single element passive beats one covering everything at a lower figure. Fires only inside a build.

rules.name: Arc gear is safer with armour that resists it
rules.say: Arc chains to whoever is closest, you included, and your armour takes most of that off you.
rules.judgement: Ours, and deliberately small: the armour does not make the weapon better, it makes its worst habit cheaper. Scales with the armour's figure. Fires only inside a build.

rules.name: Armour that resists the gas you brought
rules.say: You are bringing gas, and you will walk through your own cloud sooner or later. This armour lets you.
rules.source: The passive's own effect, read as a number. Advanced Filtration resists 80%, Acclimated 50%, Desert Stormer 40%, Hazmat 25%
rules.judgement: Ours, the curator's pairing from 4 October 2026. Scales with how much it resists, so a single element passive beats one covering everything at a lower figure. Fires only inside a build.

rules.name: Gas gear is safer with armour that resists it
rules.say: A gas cloud does not care whose it is, and your armour lets you stand in yours.
rules.judgement: Ours, and deliberately small: the armour does not make the weapon better, it makes its worst habit cheaper. Scales with the armour's figure. Fires only inside a build.

rules.name: C4 Pack beside armour that throws further
rules.say: C4 is thrown before it is set off, and this armour throws it further: further from you when it goes, and further onto the thing you wanted it on.
rules.judgement: Ours, the curator's ask of 4 October 2026, read as throw range. Named by id because nothing else is a backpack of thrown charges. Fires only inside a build.

rules.name: Throw range with a C4 Pack to throw
rules.say: You are carrying a backpack full of things to throw, and this passive throws them further.
rules.judgement: Ours. Servo-Assisted throws 30% further, Desert Stormer 20%. Fires only inside a build.

rules.name: Muscle Enhancement where the ground drags at you
rules.say: Water, mud, deep undergrowth or snow slow you down on this planet, and this booster takes most of that drag away.
rules.source: helldivers.wiki.gg, Muscle Enhancement: it reduces the slow from water, snow, mud, foliage, sandstorms, blizzards and barbed wire
rules.judgement: The ground per biome is the curator's reading, 4 October 2026, kept in the terrain table in vocabulary.json and his to correct.

rules.name: Muscle Enhancement in sandstorms and blizzards
rules.say: Sandstorms and blizzards slow you as well as blind you, and this booster takes the slow off.
rules.source: helldivers.wiki.gg, Muscle Enhancement, and the hazard text: both storms reduce mobility

rules.name: Muscle Enhancement on dry ground with no storm
rules.say: Dry, firm ground and no storm. This booster does nothing on sand, slopes or climbing, so here it is a slot spent on nothing.
rules.source: helldivers.wiki.gg, Muscle Enhancement: no benefit whatsoever on sand without weather, inclines, vaulting or tremors
rules.judgement: The ground per biome is the curator's reading, 4 October 2026, kept in the terrain table in vocabulary.json and his to correct.

rules.name: Muscle Enhancement on dry ground against the Terminids
rules.say: Dry ground and no storm, so the terrain half of this booster does nothing here. It still shortens the slow from bug acid, which is why it loses less on this front.
rules.source: helldivers.wiki.gg, Muscle Enhancement: it also covers acid from Terminid attacks and Bug Mine explosions
rules.judgement: The ground per biome is the curator's reading, 4 October 2026, kept in the terrain table in vocabulary.json and his to correct.

rules.name: The Jump Pack on steep ground
rules.say: Steep ground, and the Jump Pack's landing thrusters cancel fall damage, so a cliff is a shortcut rather than a death.
rules.source: helldivers.wiki.gg, LIFT-850 Jump Pack: no fall damage when the landing thrusters engage
rules.judgement: The ground per biome is the curator's reading, 4 October 2026, kept in the terrain table in vocabulary.json and his to correct.

rules.name: The Warp Pack on steep ground
rules.say: Steep ground. The Warp Pack carries you ten metres straight ahead and leaves you wherever that is, mid-air included, and nothing breaks the fall.
rules.source: helldivers.wiki.gg, LIFT-182 Warp Pack: a Helldiver warping in mid-air stays in mid-air and falls, potentially taking damage
rules.judgement: The ground per biome is the curator's reading, 4 October 2026, kept in the terrain table in vocabulary.json and his to correct.

rules.name: FRVs on open, even ground
rules.say: Open, even ground, where the FRV is fast and stays on its wheels.
rules.judgement: The curator's, from play: an oasis map drove easily. The ground per biome is the curator's reading, 4 October 2026, kept in the terrain table in vocabulary.json and his to correct.

rules.name: FRVs on broken, rocky or icy ground
rules.say: Broken, rocky or icy ground, where the FRV flips on a ledge it should have cleared and you end up walking anyway.
rules.judgement: The curator's, from play: snow, volcanic, rocky canyon and highland planets drive badly. Players on Steam report the same, that a small rise can roll it. The ground per biome is the curator's reading, 4 October 2026, kept in the terrain table in vocabulary.json and his to correct.

rules.name: The Jump Pack between buildings
rules.say: This planet has a megacity, so odds are you fight between buildings, and clipping one mid-jump ragdolls you and costs you the seconds you jumped to save.
rules.judgement: The curator's call from play, 4 October 2026. Some community advice disagrees and favours fighting from the rooftops; his play wins here and that view is recorded. A guess: the planet has a megacity, which does not mean this mission is in it, so this carries about half the weight a sure fact would.

rules.name: The Warp Pack between buildings
rules.say: This planet has a megacity, so odds are you fight between buildings, and the Warp Pack goes through walls where everything else has to go round.
rules.source: helldivers.wiki.gg, LIFT-182 Warp Pack: it bypasses terrain, buildings, enemies and bunker doors
rules.judgement: A guess: the planet has a megacity, which does not mean this mission is in it, so this carries about half the weight a sure fact would.

rules.name: The Warp Pack when you are alone
rules.say: Alone, a two person bunker door is shut to you. The Warp Pack goes straight through it.
rules.source: helldivers.wiki.gg, Bunker: two Helldivers press a button each, or one uses the Warp Pack to bypass the door

rules.name: The Orbital Laser on a short mission
rules.say: Three uses, five minutes apart. On a clock this short you throw every one of them, each clearing a base while you run for the next.
rules.source: helldivers.wiki.gg, Orbital Laser: 3 uses, 300 second cooldown. Time limits from each mission's article, read by npm run missions
rules.judgement: The curator's, 4 October 2026: on a forty minute mission the three are gone halfway through.

rules.name: Stamina Enhancement on a hot planet
rules.say: Intense heat halves your stamina, and this booster's extra capacity and faster recovery win a good part of it back.
rules.source: helldivers.wiki.gg, Stamina Enhancement: +22.5% max stamina and +40% regen; Intense Heat halves max stamina

rules.name: Integrated Extinguishers where the planet burns
rules.say: This planet sets people on fire whether or not anybody brought any, and this booster puts you out sooner.
rules.source: The booster's own text, and the hazard text: fire tornadoes, and volcanoes throwing burning rocks
rules.judgement: Ours.

rules.name: The Shield Generator Pack in acid storms, sandstorms and blizzards
rules.say: While it holds, the bubble also keeps out acid storms, sandstorms and blizzards. It does nothing about fire or gas.
rules.source: helldivers.wiki.gg, SH-32 Shield Generator Pack: blocks blizzards, sandstorms, acid storms and acid splash; not fire or gas

rules.name: Integrated Extinguishers with the fire you brought
rules.say: You brought fire, and sooner or later you stand in it. This puts you out faster.
rules.source: The booster's own text
rules.judgement: Ours. Throwables do not count: a thermite grenade is anti-tank, not a fire kit. Fires only inside a build.

rules.name: Explosive resistance with blasts you set off close
rules.say: You are bringing something that goes off close to you. A Helldiver already takes half of explosion damage, and this armour halves what is left.
rules.source: helldivers.wiki.gg: Helldivers take 50% of explosion damage. The passive's own effect, read as a number
rules.judgement: Ours: the close-blast tag is named by hand, since nothing published marks a weapon as one you set off close. The curator agreed the pairing, 4 October 2026. Fires only inside a build.

rules.name: Close blasts with explosion resistant armour
rules.say: Your armour takes most of the sting out of your own blast, so you can use this closer than you otherwise would dare.
rules.source: helldivers.wiki.gg: Helldivers take 50% of explosion damage
rules.judgement: Ours, through the close-blast tag, as its mirror. Fires only inside a build.

rules.name: A primary reload passive with a primary that eats ammo
rules.say: Your primary spends a long time reloading, or reloads a shell at a time, and this armour gets it done sooner.
rules.source: The passive's own effect. Reload times from each weapon's wiki infobox
rules.judgement: The curator's pairing, 4 October 2026, with the Eruptor and the shotguns as his examples. Long means 3.6 seconds or more, a round by round reload, a shotgun, or since 9 October 2026 a magazine of six or fewer with a reload of three seconds or more, which brings in the Explosive Crossbow. Fires only inside a build.

rules.name: A primary that eats ammo with a primary reload passive
rules.say: Your armour cuts this weapon's long reload, which is the part of it that gets you killed.
rules.judgement: Ours, the mirror of the above. Fires only inside a build.

rules.name: Crouched recoil reduction with a weapon you fire planted
rules.say: You brought a weapon you fire from a crouch or prone anyway, and this armour cuts the recoil in exactly that stance.
rules.source: The passive's own effect: -30% recoil crouched or prone
rules.judgement: Tentative, and the curator was not sure of it, 4 October 2026. He added the Autocannon. Named by hand. Fires only inside a build.

rules.name: Vitality Enhancement with gas resistant armour
rules.say: Your armour already shrugs off most gas, and this booster's resistance closes the rest: together you can stand in your own cloud.
rules.source: helldivers.wiki.gg, Orbital Gas Strike: Advanced Filtration with Vitality Enhancement makes a Helldiver immune to gas
rules.judgement: Ours. Fires only inside a build.

rules.name: The Stim Pistol with armour that lengthens stims
rules.say: Your armour adds two seconds to every stim, and that reaches the stims this pistol fires into your squad as well.
rules.source: helldivers.wiki.gg, Med-Kit: the longer stim duration extends to the P-11 Stim Pistol
rules.judgement: Fires only inside a build.

rules.name: Armour that lengthens stims with the Stim Pistol
rules.say: You brought the Stim Pistol, so the two extra seconds on every stim reach your whole squad, not only you.
rules.source: helldivers.wiki.gg, Med-Kit
rules.judgement: Fires only inside a build.

rules.name: The Ballistic Shield with a one handed primary
rules.say: The shield takes one hand, and your primary needs only the other, so you keep fighting with it behind the shield.
rules.source: helldivers.wiki.gg, Ballistic Shield Backpack: it needs a weapon with the One Handed trait. The trait from each weapon's infobox
rules.judgement: Fires only inside a build.

rules.name: The Ballistic Shield with a two handed primary
rules.say: The shield takes one hand, and your primary needs two, so with the shield up you fight with your sidearm.
rules.source: helldivers.wiki.gg, Ballistic Shield Backpack
rules.judgement: Fires only inside a build, and on a build with no primary yet it fires too, which is the honest reading of what you could hold.

rules.name: A one handed primary with the Ballistic Shield
rules.say: One hand on this, the other on the shield: you get to fight and stay covered at once.
rules.source: helldivers.wiki.gg, Ballistic Shield Backpack
rules.judgement: Fires only inside a build.

rules.name: Stamina Enhancement in heavy armour
rules.say: You are in heavy armour, which recovers stamina at half the rate of medium. This booster's faster recovery and deeper reserve win a lot of that back.
rules.source: helldivers.wiki.gg, Stamina Enhancement: +22.5% max stamina, +40% regen. Armor: heavy regen 50 against medium 100
rules.judgement: The curator's pairing, 4 October 2026. Reads the weight of the armour set the build wears, so it fires only inside a build that has chosen a set. The weights' numbers are the wiki's: light 550 speed and 125 stamina regen, medium 500 and 100, heavy 450 and 50.

rules.name: Dead Sprint in heavy armour
rules.say: Heavy armour runs out of stamina first, and this lets you keep running when it does, at the cost of health.
rules.judgement: Ours, after the curator's point that heavy armour wants something for its legs. knownGaps: Three visibility rules lean on a long-range tag that is our judgement rather than a published field. It lives in vocabulary.json with its reasoning, and the rules that read it carry a `judgement` saying so. It used to be the same six ids written out inside each of those three rules.

The visibility rules key on the Marksman category only. Special was tried and dropped: it holds a flamethrower, a stim pistol and a shotgun pistol alongside the Dominator, so it says nothing about range.

Armour penetration moves no rating at the item level and it must not. It moves one at the loadout level as of 1.20.0: build-rules.json reads the best thing a build holds against the front, which splits the 39 curated builds 36 / 41 / 23 where the per item reading split 51 primaries 48 to 3. Enemy armour is still shown on every expanded row as a fact. See whyThereAreNoArmourRules, which is about this file and stays true.

Suppressed is sourced from a wiki article infobox rather than from a module, so it is curated on the items instead of fetched. It is a real published fact, 13 metres of audible range on the wiki's Stealth page, and it carries no `judgement` field for that reason. fetch-wiki.mjs reads weapon infoboxes since 4 October 2026, for reload times, so moving Suppressed into the fetch is now a small change rather than a new one.

The weather rules price a hazard as if it were always happening. A planet listing sandstorms has sandstorms sometimes, roughly three minutes at a time, and nothing in the data says how often. The visibility penalties are set as a risk you carry across a run rather than a state you are in, which is a judgement and not a measurement.

Peril is 6 * (difficulty - 5) + SQUAD_PRESSURE[squad], where the squad curve is [10, 4, 1, 0] taken from the wiki patrol interval multipliers. The formula is unchanged on 4 October 2026; what changed is that the stealth rules also gate on squad. The curator: a four stack on Super Helldive knows what it is doing, so stealth is a question for one or two of you, from solo on Suicide Mission or two of you on Impossible. Peril alone puts four of you at difficulty 10 above two of you at 9, which is the wrong way round for stealth, so the squad gate does what the formula cannot.

The stealth rules scale off peril from 16, gated at 22, for one or two of you. Bugs and squids have their own, at about six tenths of the bot figure, since 4 October 2026. Nothing on bugs or squids reads difficulty for anything but stealth, so the gradient there is still thin.

The negative half is used once. easy-drop-wastes-stealth-armour takes up to half a tier off stealth passives below zero peril. The old inverted halves, silenced weapons marked down and loud ones lifted on an easy drop, were removed on 4 October 2026: not needing stealth is not a reason to mark it down. Nothing yet says that anti tank at difficulty 3 is firepower for an enemy that does not spawn.

A rule scaling off peril must not name a squad size in its say. Peril is 6 * (difficulty - 5) + SQUAD_PRESSURE[squad] and depth reaches it as readily as being alone does, so four players on Super Helldive sit at 30. All three bot peril rules shipped in 1.19.0 asserting the reader was outnumbered, and their inverted halves asserted the reader was not, both on a figure that says neither. Fixed on 22 August 2026 by describing the pressure instead. Nothing about how a squad size might get its own wording is solved here; the rule simply may not claim one it did not check.

Pairing rules, those with an alongside or notAlongside clause, read the rest of the build and so never fire on a tier row. They show in the builder's picker and slots and on every build's parts. Twenty since 4 October 2026: stealth, True Grit, Gunslinger, melee, fire, arc and gas resistance, and C4 with throw range. npm run builds measures them by placing each subject in 60 random builds.

Considered and cut by the curator on 4 October 2026, recorded so nobody rebuilds them. True Grit worth more solo, and team weapons marked down solo: the wiki says assisted reloads skip True Grit and team weapons are built for a loader, but in practice nobody team reloads, so neither changes what is worth bringing. Peak Physique paired with low ergonomics support weapons: the +30 ergonomics is real, but those weapons are better served by other passives. Kinetic Displacement or Blunt Force Mitigation paired with a Jump Pack or a vehicle: nobody should pick a passive to soften their own bad landings.

Held back for want of a source, 4 October 2026: whether Med-Kit's longer stims also lengthen Experimental Infusion, whether Localization Confusion matters more for a small squad, and how the Hover Pack fares on steep ground. Fire against the Automatons is not a gap: the wiki gives no front wide fire resistance, and the vote already prices flame's short range against a front that shoots from far away.

The city rules guess from the planet: a planet with a megacity reads as a city fight wherever the mission actually is. The scenario does not know which part of a planet a mission is on, so those rules carry half weight and say they are a guess.

Armour weight comes from the set a build wears, since 4 October 2026, and every build made before then, and every preset, has no set and so no weight. The weight rules stay silent on those rather than guessing medium, the same contract as an unset difficulty.
